extra_quotes: Ground truth is generated with the open-source TCAD solver DEVSIM 3 [19], solving the steady-state drift–diffusion system for a silicon p–n diode atT=300 K (U t =25.89 mV, ni =10 10 cm−3,ε=11.7ε 0) with constant mobilitiesµ n =1417 andµ p =470.5 cm 2/V s and equal lifetimesτ n =τ p =10 −5 s [11].

Below it, in the stiff corner of high doping and long devices (W dep ∼20 nm), the errors are 10–20 times larger than in the central bins and only about 1% of the devices fall there, too few to calibrate, so we report no interval.

Extrapolating in voltage degrades beyond that range, to a median error of 25% up to the built-in potential against 1.9% inside it, and it fails above the built-in potential, where the device enters a regime absent from the training data.

The scope of the study is limited. The detailed analysis covers one doping family, a symmetric abrupt junction with a fixed relative smearing of the doping, constant mobility, long lifetimes and forward bias only.
